cohort: 9239 nulliparous women with term, singleton, vertex live births in California between 2007 and 2012
finding: Successful operative vaginal delivery was associated with a reduction in severe maternal morbidity compared with cesarean delivery after prolonged second stage of labor, while failed operative vaginal delivery was associated with increased risks of both severe maternal and neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: In nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex births, successful operative vaginal delivery was associated with a reduced risk of severe maternal morbidity compared to cesarean delivery after prolonged second stage of labor.
